chunks: It is narrated from Abū al-Rabīʿ, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say: If an orchard containing date-palms and trees is sold for one year, then it must not be sold until its fruit reaches maturity. And if it is sold for two years or three, then there is no harm in its sale after there is some greenery in it.

key_terms.الْحَائِطُ: an orchard or enclosed garden being sold
key_terms.ثَمَرَتُهُ: its fruit, whose maturity affects the ruling

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible in Shi'i fiqh to sell the produce of an orchard for one year or for multiple years?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sale of an orchard's produce over different time periods. For a one-year sale, the fruit must have reached maturity before the sale is valid, while for a two- or three-year sale, the presence of some visible greenery is sufficient.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3903 - It is narrated from Abu Al-Rabi' who said that Abu Abdillah (as) said:

"Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) used to say: If an orchard containing palm trees and other trees is sold for one year, it should not be sold until its fruits have ripened. However, if it is sold for two or three years, then there is no harm in selling it as long as there is some greenery present in it."
